---
name: social-post
description: Write a post, caption, bio, announcement or short ad for social media or a group chat - Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, TikTok, WhatsApp groups, a marketplace listing - in the user's voice, the right length for the platform, with hashtags only where they help.
---
# Social media post

Use this when the user wants a post, a caption, a profile bio, a birthday or event announcement, a job post, a product or flat listing, or a message for a group.

Steps:
1. Get the platform, the goal (inform, sell, invite, celebrate, find someone) and the one thing the reader should do (comment, click, call, come).
2. Write the first line as the hook: the news, the offer or the question. Readers see only the first line before "more".
3. Give the facts in the body: what, when, where, how much, for whom. Facts in figures.
4. End with the call to action in one line.
5. Hashtags: 3 to 5 that a person would really search for, after the text; none on LinkedIn job posts beyond 2, none in a WhatsApp message.
6. Give one post, complete. Offer in one line to make it shorter, funnier or more formal.

Length defaults:
- X: under 280 characters. Instagram caption: 1 to 3 short paragraphs, under 150 words. LinkedIn: 80 to 200 words, one idea, line breaks between sentences. Facebook or a group: 40 to 120 words. TikTok caption: one line and 3 hashtags. A listing (flat, car, item): title under 60 characters, then 5 fact lines, then condition and contact.
- Emoji: none on LinkedIn and in listings; up to 3 elsewhere, only if the user's tone is casual.
- Voice: the user's own ("I", "we"), no marketing words ("amazing", "game-changer"), no claims the user did not make.

Output template:
<hook line>

<facts, 2 to 5 lines>

<call to action>
<hashtags, if any>

Example:
User: "Instagram caption, I finally opened my small bakery in Hamburg, opening Saturday 9am, first 50 customers get a free cinnamon bun."
Good answer: "Three years of early mornings, and the sign is finally up. / Our bakery opens this Saturday at 9:00 in Hamburg-Eimsbüttel. Sourdough, rye, cinnamon buns, all from our own oven. The first 50 customers get a cinnamon bun on us. / Come by, say hi, bring a friend. #Hamburg #Bakery #Eimsbüttel #Sourdough"

Do:
- Put the most searched fact (place, date, price) in the first two lines.
- Write it so it still makes sense without the picture.
Don't:
- Don't invent prices, dates, discounts or numbers of followers.
- Don't add "Link in bio" or a link unless the user has one.
- Don't produce five variants unless asked.

Before you answer, check: the first line stands alone as a hook; every fact the user gave is in; the length fits the platform; the call to action is one clear line; hashtags are few and real.
